title: Problem set 14: Electroactive layers and modified electrodes
summary: Practice with surface-confined redox species: coverage from peak charge, scan-rate dependence, peak width, self-assembled monolayers and charge hopping.

intro.text: A chemically modified electrode carries an intentional layer of redox, catalytic or recognition groups. For a surface-confined couple the peak current follows ip = n^2 F^2 Gamma A v/(4RT), proportional to scan rate, with an ideal half-width of 90.6/n mV.
Integrating the peak charge gives the coverage Gamma = Q/(nFA), and in polymer films charge can hop between redox sites.

blocks.text: A chemically modified electrode carries an intentional layer of redox, catalytic or recognition groups. For a surface-confined couple the peak current follows ip = n^2 F^2 Gamma A v/(4RT), proportional to scan rate, with an ideal half-width of 90.6/n mV.
Integrating the peak charge gives the coverage Gamma = Q/(nFA), and in polymer films charge can hop between redox sites.

questions.question: A surface-confined redox couple gives a peak of area 10.0 uC on a 1.0 cm2 electrode with n = 1. Calculate the surface coverage in mol/cm2 (Gamma = Q/(nFA), F = 96485 C/mol).
For an ideal surface wave the peak current is ip = n^2 F^2 Gamma A v/(4RT). Calculate ip in uA for n = 1, Gamma = 1.0e-10 mol/cm2, A = 1.0 cm2, v = 0.10 V/s, T = 298.15 K.
For an ideal surface-confined wave the peak current is proportional to scan rate v (not v^(1/2)). If the scan rate is doubled, by what factor does ip change?
questions.explanation: For a surface wave ip proportional to v, so doubling the scan rate doubles the peak current.

questions.question: The ideal full width at half maximum of a surface wave is 90.6/n mV. Calculate this width in mV for n = 2.
questions.explanation: Width = 90.6/2 = 45.3 mV. This narrow, symmetrical wave is a signature of a surface-confined couple.

questions.question: The defining kinetic signature of a surface-confined redox couple in cyclic voltammetry is that the peak current is proportional to:
options: The square root of the scan rate
The square of the scan rate
The scan rate to the power minus one
questions.explanation: With no diffusion to the surface species, ip is proportional to v, not v^(1/2). This distinguishes a surface wave from a diffusion-controlled one.

questions.question: Integrating the charge under a surface wave gives the surface coverage Gamma of the redox species.
questions.explanation: The total charge is nFA Gamma, so the peak area directly measures how many moles per unit area are attached to the electrode.

questions.question: A self-assembled monolayer (SAM) on a gold electrode is often used to:
options: Attach well-defined redox or recognition groups at a controlled coverage
Change the metal to a semiconductor
questions.explanation: Thiols assemble into a well-ordered monolayer on gold, providing a tunable, reproducible platform for attaching redox centres, catalysts or recognition elements.

questions.question: In a redox polymer film, charge can move by electron self-exchange (hopping) between adjacent redox sites.
questions.explanation: Electrons hop between neighbouring redox centres in the film, so the film behaves as an electron-transfer medium, with an apparent diffusion coefficient for charge transport.

questions.question: Which are characteristics of chemically modified electrodes? Select all that apply.
options: A deliberately attached layer of redox, catalytic or recognition species
Peak currents for surface species proportional to scan rate
Automatic loss of all electrochemical response
questions.explanation: Modified electrodes carry an intentional surface layer, give v-proportional peaks for confined species, and can catalyse reactions of solution analytes. They do not lose their response.

questions.question: If a monolayer holds 5.0e-11 mol/cm2 of a one-electron redox species on a 1.0 cm2 electrode, what charge in uC is passed in oxidising the whole layer? (Q = nF Gamma A.)
A surface-confined couple gives a peak of area 5.0 uC on a 1.0 cm2 electrode with n = 2. Calculate the coverage in mol/cm2.
For a surface-confined redox species the peak current is proportional to scan rate v. If the scan rate is increased by a factor of 4, by what factor does ip change?
questions.explanation: Since ip is proportional to v for a surface species, a factor of 4 in v gives a factor of 4 in ip (unlike v^(1/2) for a diffusing species).

questions.question: A narrow, symmetric peak with a half-width of about 90.6/n mV and ip proportional to v indicates:
questions.explanation: These are the signatures of an ideal surface wave: a symmetric, narrow peak growing linearly with scan rate.

questions.question: Self-assembled monolayers form spontaneously when thiols adsorb on a gold surface.
questions.explanation: The strong gold-sulfur bond drives thiols to organise into a dense, ordered monolayer, a convenient platform for modifying electrodes.

questions.question: Which are uses of modified electrodes? Select all that apply.
options: Immobilising a catalyst at the surface
questions.explanation: Modified electrodes immobilise catalysts, mediators and recognition groups. Melting the metal is not a purpose of surface modification.
